question: Does one spoken room-name cue change segmentation or description, on footage where the cue's wording and timing are known exactly?
one_way_note: A generated voice is clean, close-miked and unaccented. Real walkthrough narration is muffled, off-axis and half-finished. If a perfect cue produces no S1-minus-S0 lift, the audio hypothesis is dead without needing real audio; a lift here does not carry to real audio.
matched_pair_note: S0 and S1 do not need two generations. Generate the narrated clip once, then strip the audio track with ffmpeg to produce S0. The footage is then byte-identical between arms, which is a cleaner control than two renders could ever be.

clips.camera: start on the reference framing at the foot of the stairs, climb slowly and steadily, pause for about one second on a clear tread edge partway up, then continue to the landing and come to rest facing it; keep the handrail and the boxed storage in frame during the climb
intended_defects: frayed strip along the front edge of one stair tread
intended_negatives: shadow behind boxes is not damp
hidden treads are not assumed damaged

audio.cue_text: This is the stairs and landing.
audio.voice: one calm unhurried adult voice, off camera, ordinary UK domestic recording made on a phone held at chest height
audio.after_cue: room tone only; no further speech, no music, no sound effects
audio.cue_timing_rule: requested placement is a target; the gold cue timestamp is read from the delivered audio track, never assumed

gold.cue_transcript: This is the stairs and landing.
gold.scored_by: run S0 (audio stripped) and S1 (audio intact) through audio_cues.py + segment.py + curate.py + describe.py; report S1-S0 on room-name accuracy, boundary error, defect recall for the frayed tread, hero selection, and review corrections
gold.guardrail: S1 cues are soft evidence per docs/11: they may raise the probability of a nearby name but must not create a hard cut. A silent clip must reproduce S0 exactly.

clips.design_note: RP-021 carries a real enumerated defect on a tread and a deliberate occlusion (boxes). The one-second pause on a clear tread edge is the pause-detection signal from eval_pause_detect.py, so this clip exercises three consumers of audio and motion at once.
